games.title: Number Word Wizard
games.skillName: Reading and writing numbers to 20 in words
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to read and write numbers from 1 to 20 in numerals and words
games.instruction: Read the number, then tap the matching word or numeral.
games.hint: Not quite. Say the number out loud slowly, then try again.

questions.ask: Which word is the number 7?
Which word is the number 12?
Which word is the number 15?
What number is 'nineteen'?
What number is 'thirteen'?
Which is the correct spelling of 8?
Which word is the number 20?
What number is 'eleven'?
Which word is the number 4?
Which word is the number 17?

games.title: Most or Least?
games.skillName: Equal to, more than, less than, most and least
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and represent numbers using objects and pictorial representations including the number line, and use the language of: equal to, more than, less than (fewer), most, least
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Picture the numbers on a number line, then try again.

questions.ask: Which number is more than 9?
Which number is less than 6?
Which is the most: 3, 11, 8 or 5?
Which is the least: 14, 9, 17 or 12?
Which is equal to 10?
Sam has 6 sweets. Mia has 9 sweets. Who has fewer?
Ali has 7 stickers. Jo has 7 stickers. What is true?
Which number is more than 12 but less than 15?
Which group has the most?
Which number is 1 less than 20?

games.title: Hop Past 100
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to count to and across 100, forwards and backwards, beginning with 0 or 1, or from any given number
games.instruction: Count along in ones, then tap the next number.
games.hint: Not quite. Say the numbers out loud in order, then try again.

questions.ask: 98, 99, 100, ... What comes next?
103, 102, 101, ... What comes next?
97, 98, 99, ... What comes next?
Count back: 101, 100, 99, ... What comes next?
105, 106, 107, ... What comes next?
89, 90, 91, ... What comes next?
Count back: 112, 111, 110, ... What comes next?
What number comes just before 100?
What number comes just after 109?
Count back: 120, 119, 118, ... What comes next?

games.title: Heavy, Full or Quick
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to compare, describe and solve practical problems for: mass/weight [for example, heavy/light, heavier than, lighter than]; capacity and volume [for example, full/empty, more than, less than, half, half full, quarter]; time [for example, quicker, slower, earlier, later]
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Imagine holding, filling or racing them, then try again.

questions.ask: Which of these is the heaviest?
Which of these is the lightest?
A jug has no water in it at all. It is...
A cup is filled right up to the top. It is...
A bath is filled up to the middle. It is...
Which animal is the quickest?
Tom runs a race in 10 seconds. Ann takes 15 seconds. Who is quicker?
Which meal happens earliest in the day?
On a balance, the side with the books goes down. Which is heavier?
Which is later in the same afternoon?

games.title: Coin Counter
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise and know the value of different denominations of coins and notes
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Look at the number on each coin or note, then try again.

questions.ask: Which coin is worth the most?
Which coin is worth the least?
Which of these is a note, not a coin?
How many pence is a £1 coin worth?
Which coin is worth more than 20p?
Which coin is worth the same as two 5p coins?
Which note is worth the most?
Which coin is worth the same as two £1 coins?
Which coin is worth less than 5p?

games.title: Days and Months
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to sequence events in chronological order using language [for example, before and after, next, first, today, yesterday, tomorrow, morning, afternoon and evening]; recognise and use language relating to dates, including days of the week, weeks, months and years
games.instruction: Think about the order, then tap what comes next.
games.hint: Not quite. Say the days or months in order from the start, then try again.

questions.ask: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, ... What comes next?
What day comes after Saturday?
What day comes before Friday?
January, February, March, ... What comes next?
Which month comes after December?
If today is Tuesday, what day was yesterday?
If today is Sunday, what day is tomorrow?
Planting a seed: what do you do first?
How many days are in a week?
Which part of the day comes first?

games.title: Shape Spotter
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise and name common 2-D and 3-D shapes, including: 2-D shapes [for example, rectangles (including squares), circles and triangles]
games.instruction: Read the clues, then tap the shape.
games.hint: Not quite. Count the sides and corners in the clue, then try again.

questions.ask: I have 3 straight sides and 3 corners. What am I?
I am round and have no corners. What am I?
I have 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. What am I?
I have 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short, and 4 square corners. What am I?
I have no straight sides at all. Which shape am I?
A bicycle wheel is shaped like me. What am I?
A door is usually shaped like me. What am I?
I am the only one of these with 3 corners. What am I?
I am a rectangle with all 4 sides the same length. What am I?
